turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mrs Cartwright? Come on through. I'll grab your observations before the doctor sees you, if that's alright.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Of course. Thank you for fitting me in today.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Pop your arm out for me. That's one hundred and forty-eight over eighty-six.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I beg your pardon — could you repeat the lower number?
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Eighty-six. Pulse is seventy-two, nice and steady. Weight's seventy-one kilograms.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I see. Thank you very much.
[SEG0007] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Doctor's just finishing a note on the computer. Take a seat, she won't be long.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Helen — sorry, this computer's having a moment. It's the routine review, yeah?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, Doctor. It is a routine review, though I did wish to raise the matter of my tablets.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Give me a second, the screen's jumped back to someone else. What was that?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I wished to raise my tablets, Doctor.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. You're on ramipril for the blood pressure.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): I am, yes. Though not quite as it was prescribed, I am afraid.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): How do you mean?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I have been taking it every other day. I thought that might be kinder to me.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Every other day. And the dose — remind me, the list won't load.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Five milligrams of ramipril. I had a moment of thinking it was ten, but the packet clearly says five. And, as I said, every other day.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Five milligrams, every second day. How long have you been doing that?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Some months, I should think. I couldn't give you a proper date. Perhaps since last winter, or the winter before. It rather blurs.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): OK. And the cholesterol tablet, the atorvastatin?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I stopped that.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry — you stopped which one? Say it again, the fan in this room is dreadful.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): The cholesterol tablet. Atorvastatin. I stopped it entirely.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Forty milligrams, that was the dose on the script. When did you stop?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I read an article online about muscle damage, and I became quite anxious. It was around Diwali — my neighbour puts the lights out — or perhaps after...
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): So not a month you can point to.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Last winter, or the one before that. I am sorry to be so vague.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Don't be. Any muscle pain, before you stopped or since?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No muscle pain at all. I stopped from worry, not because I felt unwell.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain? Breathlessness?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): My husband has been rather tired, actually. His diabetes tablets sit in the same cupboard, and I did wonder —
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's him, not you. For you — any chest pain, or short of breath?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Neither of those. I do apologise for answering the wrong question.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Easy done. Any cough? And any dizziness?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough. I am a little light-headed if I stand up too quickly. I don't think my ankles have been swelling, but I may be wrong.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): The light-headed feeling — how long has that been going on?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): A few weeks. Perhaps six. I am not entirely sure when it began.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are you checking your pressure at home?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I haven't a machine of my own. There is one in the house, but it belongs to my husband, for his diabetes reviews. Those readings are his, not mine.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): What diabetes medicine is he on? I only want to be sure the bottles aren't getting mixed.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Metformin, I believe. Five hundred milligrams, twice a day. I have never taken his tablets.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Anything else of yours — aspirin, something from the chemist, a supplement?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): No other tablets. I have a cup of tea in the afternoon and nothing stronger, and I have never smoked.
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll take the tea and the smoking, even though I asked about medicines. Any allergies — medicines, foods, anything?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I am aware of.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): The blood pressure and the cholesterol — how long have those been with you?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): The high blood pressure for many years. The high cholesterol was found around the same period. I have had no operations.
[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): Family history? The cursor's in the wrong box. Say it again slowly, would you?
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): My mother had a stroke. She was in her seventies.
[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): Heart disease or diabetes in the family, apart from your husband?
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that I know of. My father lived to eighty-nine, which I have always been grateful for.
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll have a quick listen while this page loads. Heart sounds are normal and the chest is clear. No swelling at the ankles. The pulses in your feet are fine.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): I am very glad to hear that.

[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Today's pressure is one forty-eight over eighty-six, a bit above where I'd like it. Probably from taking the ramipril every other day. I was going to leave the statin off and just see you in three months with the usual bloods.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Would three months be soon enough, Doctor, given that I stopped it?

[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Actually, scratch that. You've been off it for goodness knows how long, and the pressure's up. We'll do the bloods now — cholesterol, kidney function, and a sugar — and I'll see you in a month to decide about the statin.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. I ought not to have stopped it on the strength of a website.

[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm not going to tell you off. Plenty of people read things online. What I'd like is the ramipril, five milligrams, every day again. If the dizziness picks up, ring the surgery — don't just start skipping doses.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Every day. Yes, I can manage that.

[SEG0060] person_3 (DOCTOR): Don't restart the atorvastatin yourself. We'll look at the numbers and revisit that decision in a month. If the kidney results are off we might change the ramipril dose, but only if they say so.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): Shall I attend the pathology room downstairs?
[SEG0062] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. The form is for lipids, U and Es, and an HbA1c. Fasting if you can manage it, but don't skip the test if you can't.
[SEG0063] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry to butt in, Doctor — reception's chasing the next slot. I can book Mrs Cartwright while I'm here.
[SEG0064] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Not the three months I said earlier — one month. The blood form should be on the printer.
[SEG0065] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Four weeks, then. Would you rather morning or later in the day?
[SEG0066] person_2 (PATIENT): A morning would be preferable, if you have one free.
[SEG0067] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Nine fifteen, four weeks from today. I'll leave the form at the desk for you.
[SEG0068] person_3 (DOCTOR): Helen — did you mention a headache earlier? I may have clicked into the wrong note.
[SEG0069] person_2 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. I did not mention a headache. I have not had one.
[SEG0070] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right, ignore me. Any questions before the screen freezes again?
[SEG0071] person_2 (PATIENT): Only to confirm: the metformin remains my husband's, and I telephone the surgery if the daily ramipril makes me more light-headed.
[SEG0072] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's exactly it. A walk most days is plenty, and a bit less salt. Nothing drastic.
[SEG0073] person_2 (PATIENT): I already walk to the shops, and my knees are quite alright, so that is no trouble at all. Thank you for being so patient.
[SEG0074] person_3 (DOCTOR): You were right to tell me. See you in a month, and we'll sort the statin once those bloods are back.

spec.situation: Patient on routine review who admits stopping the cholesterol tablet after reading something online, still takes the BP tablet but 'every other day'; mentions husband's diabetes pills; doctor does not scold, plans repeat blood tests and revisits the statin decision in a month.
features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: High cholesterol supported, but duration stated only as around same period, not explicitly many years.
